records.text: The Lost Barrens Kodo is one of the kodo creatures found in the Barrens. It charges when it enters combat.
The Greater Barrens Kodo is a larger Barrens kodo. It charges when it enters combat.
The Barrens Kodo is a kodo creature found in the Barrens. In combat, it can use a forceful Kodo Stomp.
The Wooly Kodo is a kodo found in the Barrens. It charges when it enters combat.
Stormhide is a beast of the Barrens whose lightning glands are sought for brewing. In combat, it uses Lizard Bolt.
A beast of the Barrens that hurls a Lizard Bolt at its foes.
A beast named Stormsnout who casts Lizard Bolt.
A Savannah Patriarch, a beast.
A Zhevra Runner, a beast.
A savannah lion of the Barrens. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet wants savannah lion tusks, along with other ingredients, for his stormstout brew.
An ornery plainstrider of the Barrens, a bird usually found roaming the open country. When badly hurt, it turns desperate.
A quick-moving plainstrider of the Barrens, this bird ranges widely across the region. If a threat draws near, it can respond with a spell.
A giraffe of the Barrens, this creature roams the region's open country. It can answer an attack with a spell.
A greater thunderhawk of the Barrens, this bird is found in a few parts of the region. It can unleash a thunderclap while fighting.
A silithid creeper found around southern Barrens country, this insect lays an egg and can cast Silithid Creeper Egg.
Silithid Swarmers are beasts that set a swarm upon their foes in combat.
A Silithid Harvester is a rare creature that answers an attack with a spell.
A Sunscale Lashtail is a beast that lashes at its foes.
Sunscale Screechers are beasts whose shriek calls for help.
A Sunscale Scytheclaw is a beast that can use Thrash.
A Bristleback Hunter is a Bristleback combatant who fights with ranged attacks.
Mangletooth targets Bristleback Water Seekers among the Bristlebacks’ spiritual leaders in his conflict with them. A Water Seeker can use Frost Nova.
A Bristleback spiritual leader whom Mangletooth wants weakened so the Razormane can defeat the tribe. It wields Thorns and Entangling Roots, and when near defeat it flees to find help.
A Bristleback Geomancer, one of the tribe's spiritual leaders, whom Mangletooth wants weakened so the Razormane can overcome the Bristlebacks. It hurls Fireballs.
A Razormane Hunter, a quilboar of the tribe that raids Horde supply lines from Durotar. Thork regards the Razormane as enemies and wants them weakened. It shoots from a distance.
A Razormane Defender, a quilboar of the tribe whose raids on a Durotar caravan Thork wants ended. It bellows a Demoralizing Shout to weaken its foes.
A Razormane Water Seeker, a quilboar of the tribe Thork wants cut down for raiding Horde supply lines from Durotar. It fights with Creeping Mold.
A Razormane quilboar of the Thornweavers, whose tribe attacks the Crossroads supply lines. It casts Faerie Fire and surrounds itself with Thorns.
A Razormane geomancer among the raiders sought by Thork after attacks on a Durotar caravan. It keeps Frost Armor active while out of combat.
Elder Mystic Razorsnout is a Razormane spellcaster who uses Healing Wave and Earthbind Totem as a fight turns against them.
A Razormane mystic who maintains a Lightning Shield while out of combat.
A Kolkar wrangler who attacks at range with Shoot.
A Kolkar stormer that hurls Lightning Bolt in combat and answers an opponent’s attack with a Lightning Cloud.
Kolkar Pack Runners fight with Battle Shout and call for Verog to be summoned as they fall.
Kolkar Marauders use Strike in battle and call for Verog to be summoned as they fall.
Witchwing Harpies treat opponents as easy prey, threatening to shred them with their talons and take their heads as trophies.
Witchwing Roguefeathers threaten to shred opponents with their talons and take their heads as trophies, calling them easy prey. They use Slowing Poison in battle.
Witchwing Slayers call opponents easy prey, threatening to shred them with their talons and claim their heads as trophies.
Witchwing Ambushers call opponents easy prey, threatening to shred them with their talons and claim their heads as trophies.
Witchwing Windcallers taunt their prey with threats of torn flesh and trophies, treating a fight as a hunt. Their confidence is predatory, and they press the attack with their talons.
A Venture Co. mercenary who spots a stolen shredder and urgently calls for it to be stopped, fearing Lugwizzle will have their hides. He is more afraid of the boss's anger than of the theft itself.
A Venture Co. Enforcer is company muscle, quick to answer a fight with a forceful attack.
A Venture Co. Drudger reacts sharply when someone comes too close, warning, “Get away from there!”
A Venture Co. Peon answers an unwanted approach with a blunt warning: “Get away from there!”
A Venture Co. Overseer is an armed supervisor; when pressed in combat, he reaches for his poisoned dagger.

Brewmaster Drohn makes Chen Stormstout’s brews in Ratchet, carrying on recipes passed down from Chen through Drohn’s mentor. Chen’s Empty Keg brings back memories of the old trogg ale and the last time Drohn drank enough to black out. He remembers Chen traveling with Rexxar long ago and had not heard from him in a very long time. Drohn welcomes the chance to make the brews again and offers more when supplied with ingredients.
Sludge Beast is a rare ooze associated with the Barrens.

Kargal Battlescar handles recruitment for Barrens duty from his outpost. He respects Takrin’s scouting and agrees to sign the recruitment letter, though he says the Horde needs someone at the Crossroads more. He is openly skeptical of Sergra Darkthorn, calling her a nasty shaman and questioning Thrall’s confidence in her; he leaves the recruit to judge her for themself.

Sergra Darkthorn trains hunters at the Crossroads, treating the Barrens' plainstriders and raptors as both threats to supplies and lessons in the hunt. She sends trainees after Echeyakee and other prey, but asks them to consider the lives they take; she worries that needless killing can bring more trouble than it solves.

Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun leads the Thalo'dan Privateers from Ratchet. After Northwatch Hold's forces sink another ship from his fleet, he calls for a reprisal against their soldiers and commanders. He also welcomes the return of Gilthares Firebough, thought lost, and honors those who helped bring the privateer home.

Gann Stonespire walks alone, seeking to defend his honor and drive his enemies from his land. He regards Bael Modan’s excavation as a violation of his tribe’s ancestral home. After diplomacy fails, he pursues its leader and works to halt the destruction, including by turning the dig’s explosives against its military strength.
A Bael'dun excavator works at the Barrens dig site. Gann singles out excavators among the workers whose activity tears into his ancestral lands.
A Bael'dun foreman works at the Barrens excavation. Gann identifies foremen among those driving the digging that damages his ancestral lands.
A Bael'dun soldier serves among the site's armed force. Gann says soldiers in the Keep hold supplies used in the explosive charge he is preparing against the operation.
A Bael'dun rifleman serves among the site's armed force. Gann says riflemen in the Keep hold supplies used in the explosive charge he is preparing against the operation.

A Bael'dun officer stationed in the Barrens, this armed officer uses nimble reflexes when combat begins. The available records identify the role and combat behavior but provide no further personal history or duties.

A Burning Blade bruiser found in the Barrens, this combatant attacks with a bruising strike when a fight begins. The records establish the bruiser role and fighting behavior, but offer no individual history or personal ties.

A Burning Blade acolyte encountered in the Barrens, this combatant uses fire magic in a fight. The records establish the acolyte role and combat spell, but do not describe personal beliefs, history or relationships.

A Southsea brigand at the pirates' camp in the Barrens, this raider fights with a backhand strike. Gazlowe's complaint and bounty identify the brigands as part of the Southsea Freebooters, who raid trade ships and steal cargo; that account describes Gazlowe's grievance, not this brigand's own views.

A Southsea cannoneer at the pirates' camp in the Barrens, a ranged fighter. Gazlowe names the cannoneers among the Southsea Freebooters who raid his ships and steal his goods; that does not show this cannoneer's own motives.

A Southsea cutthroat found among the Southsea pirates in the Barrens, this combatant attacks with a close strike. The available records establish the role and fighting behavior, but give no personal history, relationships or stated views.
A Southsea Privateer, a humanoid.
Theramore Marines serve as military troops of Theramore.
Theramore Preservers are healers who wield holy magic, mending with Renew and striking foes with Holy Smite.

Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo guides hunters through trials against the beasts of the Barrens. He values strength, courage and honor, teaching that true hunters continue striving throughout their lives. He urges temperance in using strength and sees regret as a path to wisdom, and pain as a source of strength. He knows the habits and dangers of local beasts, including Ishamuhale and the thunder lizards.

Mahren Skyseer is a hunter who treats the great water beasts along the Barrens coast as worthy, honorable prey. She says she does not fear Isha Awak, despite the danger the creature poses to humans, and speaks of the hunt with reverence for its spirit. Her brother Jorn sends proven hunters to her to learn the ways of sea-beast hunting; she respects those whom he has judged ready and urges them farther along the hunter’s path.

Regthar Deathgate is a Horde warrior directing a campaign against the Kolkar centaurs in the Barrens. He sees their growing strength and incursions as a threat to Horde holdings, and orders their leaders killed to disrupt their forces. He also recruits agents for a mission into Desolace, where he believes the Kolkar threat must be addressed at its source. His reports and orders focus on the military danger to the Horde; he praises those who defeat the invaders.

Apothecary Helbrim is a Forsaken alchemist at the Crossroads, studying how the Barrens’ oasis waters alter local plants and beasts. He gathers fungal spores, renders them into an emulsion, and sends it to his associate Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff for further processing. He also sees toxic creature hearts as promising material for advancing poison research, and says the Forsaken honor their contracts.

Gazlowe runs a trading operation in Ratchet and is sharply frustrated by Southsea Freebooters raiding his ships and taking his goods. He tracks missing shipments through his ledger and the dockmaster’s records, and urgently wants a telescopic lens for his observatory alongside recovered cargo. Once the goods are returned, he thanks the helper and openly offers paid work in his operation. He has also seen the pirate ship Heedless at sea and is glad its captain will no longer trouble his ships.

Prospector Khazgorm is an Explorers' League prospector who also offers goods for sale. Gann's account identifies him as the leader of the Bael'dun excavation and seeks his journal as part of the effort to drive the dwarves from the site.

Captain Fairmount is a Northwatch captain named by Ratchet captain Thalo'thas Brightsun among the officers he wants defeated at Northwatch Hold. Her native combat abilities include rallying herself with a battle shout and interrupting a target with a pummel.

Barak Kodobane is a Kolkar centaur leader who rallies his people. Regthar Deathgate calls him a threat to Tauren holdings and places his camp near the Forgotten Pools. He fights with a net and ranged attacks.

Hezrul Bloodmark leads the Kolkar centaurs in the Barrens. Regthar describes him as fierce, brutal, and cunning, and says he leads his people from Lushwater Oasis. He urges Kolkar to act like their people and warns that orcs and their allies are close.
A Kolkar combatant whose dying cry calls for Verog. In battle, the Bloodcharger uses bloodlust and corruption.
Gesharahan is a rare creature found in the Barrens.
General Twinbraid is a humanoid general.
The Savannah Huntress is a predator of the savannah, found across several parts of the Barrens.
The Savannah Matriarch is a powerful savannah creature that calls a Savannah Cub into battle, linking its presence to the young of its kind.

Kirge Sternhorn welcomes a traveler with a prophecy and urges them toward the Crossroads, where tauren and orc lives have become intertwined. He directs the traveler to seek Thork and help the orcs, expressing confidence that they are destined for great things.

Feegly claims the Tear of the Moons as his own and still wants its power back. He says General Twinbraid grew jealous, locked the relic away in the Keep, and drove him off. His repeated demands for the Tear and exultation over its power show how fixated he remains on recovering it.

Korran is an observer sent to the Crossroads by his masters in Orgrimmar. He studies the silithid of the Field of Giants, gathering eggs and specimens to learn more about their intelligence and nature. Reports from travelers have convinced him that the creatures pose a greater threat than his masters first expected, and he seeks a reliable courier to carry his findings to Belgrom Rockmaul. Moktar also keeps an eye on him, though Korran regrets that Moktar spends more time watching his warband than fighting.

Thork leads the Crossroads' defenses in the Warchief's name and welcomes newcomers who respect the settlement. He is concerned with the safety of its people and supply lines, which Razormane attacks have put under pressure. While his scouts seek the raiders' leader, he asks for help disrupting their attacks and recovering lost supplies. Once a scout identifies Kreenig Snarlsnout as the leader, Thork directs a focused response against him and the tribe.

Mangletooth is a captive Razormane who bargains with the Horde for help against the rival Bristlebacks and against Razormane raiders who turned on him. He insists his tribe is stronger and sees its struggle through the spiritual power of Agamaggan, whose blood and bones he describes as shaping the land. Though caged and cut off from his power, he claims knowledge of blood-shard magic and offers conditional blessings.
Grenthar is a humanoid who has tasks for travelers.

Mankrik is a Horde soldier searching for his missing wife after they were separated in a battle with the Razormane. He remains at the Crossroads seeking help, and his grief has become a fierce desire for revenge against the quilboars. Thork considers that rage clouding Mankrik’s judgment, a rebuke Mankrik resents despite respecting Thork as a leader.

Tatternack Steelforge is an orc weapons researcher carrying out the Warchief’s orders to study arms and the cultures of the Barrens. His investigation into Razormane weapons has shown him that the quilboars are more skilled than he expected, making them a threat the Horde should not underestimate. He is also examining unusual ore from Thousand Needles, hoping it may yield a strong weapon for the Warchief.
Nak is named among three Razormane quilboars who left the Kraul to lead raids against the Horde. Mangletooth identifies Nak, Kuz, and Lok Orcbane as targets.
Lok Orcbane fights with Hamstring. Mangletooth names him as the warrior leading Nak and Kuz in Razormane raids against the Horde, and describes the three as ruthless and cunning.
Kuz fights with Frostbolt and Fire Blast.
Thork identifies Kreenig Snarlsnout as a quilboar leading Razormane raids on caravans from Durotar. He seeks Kreenig’s death to end the attacks.

Wizzlecrank speaks from a stolen goblin shredder he is still learning to operate. He panics when questioned about its missing key and pretends there is a mechanical fault. Impressed that the Venture Company’s machine is better than his own side’s, he wants to bring it to Sputtervalve in Ratchet and asks for protection while escaping.

Sputtervalve is a Tinkers' Union engineer directing its shredder development program under deadlines set by the Union. He is investigating unfamiliar machinery, including a samophlange and a Glowing Shard, and recruits help with the work. His dealings also include salvage coordination and Union assignments concerning engineers working for the Venture Company.

Grub cooks and sells food near the Crossroads. He offers to make dig-rat stew and asks for rats from Bael Modan; his cheerful pitch pairs the local cooking task with a rough joke about adventurers and rats.
The dig rat is a small Barrens animal hunted for meat. Grub describes them as suitable for stew, though his cooking advice is distinctly unappealing.
Supervisor Lugwizzle is a humanoid supervisor in the control room atop a derrick in the Barrens. He holds the ignition key for a shredder, which Wizzlecrank needs to get away.

Mebok Mizzyrix is a Ratchet goblin who turns Barrens curiosities into commercial experiments. After his raptor-horn “smart drink” failed, he pursued Wailing Essence for a new recipe. He studies how oasis water alters local herbs for exploitable properties and sees deliveries as a way to profit through his contacts. He calls helpers partners and offers first notice if his research finds something valuable.

Tonga Runetotem is a druid investigating the new Barrens oases and the fissures he believes may be sustaining them. He studies how their waters affect local life, from testing infertile seeds to examining snapjaw shells, and admits the mystery is too large for him to solve alone. His work joins ecological concern with patient, open-ended research.

Darsok Swiftdagger organizes the Horde’s response to harpy attacks on its caravans. He has studied the harpies’ chain of command and targets its lower ranks before their lieutenants, treating the campaign as a deliberate effort to weaken their leadership. His response is severe: after learning that the raids are revenge for Rexxar’s killing of a harpy, he orders Serena Bloodfeather killed and her head displayed to the next caravan.

Serena Bloodfeather is a harpy whom Darsok identifies as the sister of Bloodfeather, slain by Rexxar. He attributes the attacks on Horde caravans to revenge for her sister’s death, placing Serena at the center of that conflict.

Wharfmaster Dizzywig manages Ratchet’s port records and keeps track of trade between Ratchet and Booty Bay. He checks his logs when Gazlowe asks about a missing shipment and can pass along news of goods from Undermine. He also proposes splitting the sale of a large emerald with the person who retrieves it, showing his interest in trade and profit.

Cannoneer Smythe keeps watch for ships and other possible threats. His warnings show a hair-trigger approach: he treats a possible Orc vessel, an uncertain sighting, or even a sea giant as reason to fire, though he sometimes calls for a warning round. His lines convey an alert but rash defender, quick to mistake what appears on the horizon for an enemy.

Cannoneer Whessan serves as an alert defender at Northwatch Hold, calling out raiders and invaders from different directions and ordering her side to fire. Her brief warnings focus on spotting threats, while her title marks her as one of the hold’s cannoneers.
A Razormane Pathfinder, a ranged fighter of the Razormane who shoots from a distance.
A Razormane Stalker is a close-quarters fighter among the Razormane, striking opponents with a quick, practiced attack.
A Razormane Seer supports the fight with totem magic, including a Searing Totem and a Healing Ward. Its role combines offensive magic with aid for its side.
A Razormane Warfrenzy is a combatant among the Razormane. It uses a combat spell.
The Oasis Snapjaw is a creature found around the oases. It is an animal rather than a speaking character, and defends itself by slinging dirt at attackers.
A giraffe of the Barrens, this creature roams the local grasslands and can lash out when threatened.

Gazrog handles security concerns for the Crossroads. He wants the silver stolen from the guard tower returned, and believes the raptors responsible should be stopped; reports of their silver cache have made him reconsider how intelligent they may be. He also passes along troubling news about Dogran, a wounded prisoner, while keeping it from Dogran's mate, Zankaja.

Gilthares Firebough is a deckhand from Ratchet who survived the sinking of his ship and imprisonment at Northwatch Hold. Resentful of the Theramore zealots who branded him an Alliance threat, he asks for help escaping and returning to Ratchet. During the journey he warns that Southsea Freebooters hold the coast and may make the escape difficult.
A zhevra courser of the Barrens, this creature ranges through the local grasslands and can lash out when threatened.
Baron Longshore is a Southsea Freebooter captain from Gilneas, wanted by Gazlowe on charges of piracy.
Rathorian is a named hostile demon in the Barrens. He is a formidable combatant who casts a spell while fighting.
Tinkerer Sniggles is a hostile tinkerer tied to the samophlange control console: a key from him is needed to unlock it. He casts a spell when attacked.
Washte Pawne is a named beast found in the Barrens.
Owatanka is a beast of the Barrens whose electrically charged tailspike throws sparks when touched. A dangerous foe, it casts Chained Bolt in combat.
Lakota'mani is a named beast of the Barrens. Its hoof is described as a symbol of the strength of a great kodo, giving this creature a lasting association with kodo strength.
Isha Awak is a beast.
Hraq is a blacksmithing-supplies merchant who offers goods and repairs.
Traugh is a blacksmithing trainer who offers instruction. His greeting invokes the spirits and says their bringing you to him makes him feel blessed.
Nargal Deatheye is a weaponsmith who sells weapons and offers repairs.
Moorane Hearthgrain is a baker who offers goods for sale.
Barg is a general-supplies merchant who sells goods.
Tari'qa is a trade supplies merchant in the Crossroads. Visitors can browse her goods.
Jahan Hawkwing is a leather and mail armor merchant in the Crossroads. He trades with travelers and hunters; his business is lively, and he expects to sell goods brought from Thunder Bluff.

Kil'hala is a troll tailor at the Crossroads who trains tailoring. He makes a nether-lace robe using hair gathered from laughing sisters, acknowledging that they likely would not give it willingly. He describes the finished robe as comfortable, durable, and imbued with the hair's magic, and asks that Deino hear whether it suits its wearer.
Wrahk is a tailoring supplies merchant in the Crossroads.
Halija Whitestrider is a clothier in the Crossroads. Her services include selling goods and repairing equipment.
Kalyimah Stormcloud sells bags and sacks in the Crossroads.
Uthrok is a bowyer and gunsmith in the Crossroads, supplying weapons and ammunition. His services suit travelers preparing for the road through the Barrens.

Zargh is a butcher at the Crossroads who sells provisions for travel through the Barrens. He has choice cuts of meat he wants sent to Gryshka, the Orgrimmar innkeeper he calls a friend. His delivery request brings the traveler into contact with her; Zargh later asks whether she liked the meat and jokes that he may invite the courier to his wedding.
Hula'mahi supplies reagents, herbs and poison supplies at the Crossroads, serving travelers and practitioners in need of those goods.
Ironzar is a weaponsmith who sells weapons and offers repairs in the Crossroads.
Vexspindle is an armor merchant in the Crossroads, offering cloth and leather armor as well as repairs.
Grazlix is an armorer and shieldcrafter in the Crossroads, selling armor and offering repairs.

Tinkerwiz is an engineering trainer. The goblin settlement’s engineering specialist teaches the profession and directs aspiring specialists to Nixx Sprocketspring in Gadgetzan or Tinkmaster Overspark in Ironforge for further instruction.
Gagsprocket supplies engineering materials. As an engineering supplies merchant, he helps local engineers stock up on the components and equipment their work requires.
Fuzruckle is the settlement’s banker. He provides access to customers’ bank storage, serving the practical financial needs of people passing through this goblin outpost.
Kilxx is a fisherman who sells food. His fishing trade gives visitors a source of provisions in the goblin settlement.
Jazzik sells general supplies in the goblin settlement, providing everyday goods to its residents and visitors.
Ranik sells trade supplies in the goblin settlement, helping visitors and local traders find the goods needed for commerce.
A standard Horde guard stationed across several Barrens areas.

A Ratchet bruiser who speaks with open menace and contempt when confronting trouble. He insists that bloodshed has no place on neutral ground and orders miscreants out, presenting himself as an enforcer of Ratchet’s peace.

Ak’Zeloth is Neeru’s assistant at Far Watch Post and handles the next step in Neeru’s effort against the Demon Seed. He explains that power stones can disrupt its connection to the Burning Legion, directs the traveler to carry one to the altar, and warns that it will lose power with time. He can sense the Seed’s power while it remains.
Zizzek sells fishing supplies in the Barrens and invites visitors to browse his goods.
Devrak is the Crossroads wind rider master, offering paid flights to Orgrimmar and Thunder Bluff. He describes his wind riders as trained for fast travel through the Barrens’ hot air.
Lizzarik is a weapon dealer in the Barrens, loudly pitching blades and maces as the finest selection around. He urges passersby to buy quickly and offers his stock through his shop.
Jorb is a humanoid, Lizzarik's bodyguard.

Crane Operator Bigglefuzz recounts how an overloaded morning shipment from Booty Bay toppled at the docks. He saw Mad Magglish flee with a bottle of 99-year-old port and chased him to the Wailing Caverns, but would not enter. The bottle was meant as Baron Revilgaz's gift to Gazlowe, and Bigglefuzz feared losing his job over its loss.
Vrang Wildgore is a weaponsmith and armorcrafter who offers goods for browsing.
Kiknikle is a stylish clothier who offers goods to browse and access to a bank.
Pizznukle is a leather armor merchant who offers goods for browsing.

Krulmoo Fullmoon trains leatherworkers. He knows his blue leather draws attention and worries that eager recruits hunt with more enthusiasm than wisdom, so he takes precautions. His words mix a craftsman's pride in his materials with concern for the risks faced by inexperienced hunters.
Mahani is a tailor who welcomes visitors to her tent and offers tailoring training. Her greeting is polite and open, inviting visitors to ask for assistance.
Gahroot is a butcher who sells meat and provisions.

Innkeeper Boorand Plainswind warmly welcomes visitors, comparing that welcome to the wind across the plains. As an innkeeper, he offers a place to make one's home and goods to browse; a seasonal Trick or Treat interaction is also available.

Sarilus Foulborne is an undead mage whom Sentinel Velene Starstrike accuses of defiling water elementals and threatening the waters of the Barrens. In combat he conjures elementals and hurls frost magic.

Seereth Stonebreak is a shaman who hears the suffering spirits of Stonetalon and seeks to stop the Venture Company’s destruction of its forests. Many spirit whispers remain unclear, but a vision identifies the shredders XT:4 and XT:9 as threats. Seereth advocates violent resistance in the Horde’s name while believing that tauren elders’ wisdom is needed to calm the spirits, and refers allies to Magatha in Thunder Bluff.
Hecklefang Stalkers are beasts found across several areas.
Hecklefang Snarlers are beasts found across several areas.
A Kolkar Packhound is a hound of the Kolkar that fights with a special attack.
An arctic wolf kept as a riding mount.
Aean Swiftriver is a named Alliance Outrunner.
Thora Feathermoon is a named Alliance Outrunner.
Hannah Bladeleaf is a named Alliance Outrunner.
Marcus Bel is a named Alliance Outrunner.

Uzzek is a veteran warrior at Far Watch Post who instructs young warriors in combat. He teaches defense as protection for the Horde's weaker members, and wants would-be students to prove their toughness against the thunder lizards of Thunder Ridge by bringing back singed scales.
Brontus is a powerful beast that charges when a fight begins and pierces its foes' armor.
Humar the Pridelord is a powerful creature that uses Agonizing Pain when a foe comes within close range.
Snort the Heckler is a particularly dangerous beast that spits toxin at its foes.
Sister Rathtalon commands wind and lightning, buffeting foes with gusts and calling a Lightning Cloud. When badly hurt, she flees to find help.
Thunderstomp is a particularly dangerous creature that attacks with Chained Bolt.
Azzere the Skyblade is a beast that attacks with Fireball and Flame Spike.
Foreman Grills is a foreman who, when hard pressed, grabs for his poisoned dagger.
Engineer Whirleygig is an engineer who fights with gadgets, launching Explosive Sheep and a Compact Harvest Reaper.
Stonearm is a rare humanoid of the Barrens who may carry centaur bracers, which Regthar Deathgate wants taken from Kolkar warriors.
Brokespear throws weapons at his foes and fights with Slowing Poison.
Rocklance fights with Cleave and Sunder Armor.
Takk the Leaper is a named beast.
Heggin Stonewhisker is the Bael'dun Chief Engineer. He has tasks for travelers and shoots from a distance.
Malgin Barleybrew is the Bael'dun Morale Officer and sells goods to visitors. When attacked, he uses Battle Shout.
Digger Flameforge is an excavation specialist who closes in to fight and hits with a backhand.
Captain Gerogg Hammertoe is the Bael'dun Captain of the Guard, a guard leader with tasks for travelers.
Hagg Taurenbane is a Razormane champion and a direct fighter who uses Hamstring and Demoralizing Shout.
Geopriest Gukk’rok is a named creature whose combat abilities include Power Word: Shield, Renew, and Heal. He casts these spells as his health falls, including Heal below 20%.
Swinegart Spearhide is a humanoid in the Barrens.
Dishu is a rare beast of the Barrens that calls savannah cubs to its aid when a fight begins.
Larhka is a beverage merchant who offers goods for browsing.

Thun’grim Firegaze is a Horde blacksmith whose poor eyesight is central to his work. Razormane quilboar stole forged steel bars from his camp, and he asks for their recovery in return for a weapon. He also commissions armor, describing the difficulty of writing its instructions with near-blind eyes. His work includes forging and preparing armor.

Brine lives alone in a hut deep in the Barrens, surrounded by the threat of quilboar. She studies water as part of a water rite, sending initiates to gather samples from places where it sustains life. She regards even the scarce pond below her hut as precious and explains that water is sacred to the quilboar too. Brine once traveled with companions to Hillsbrad Foothills, where they fought humans before reaching Tarren Mill; she remembers its spring as a holy vestige amid the plague. She welcomes initiates into her kind and expects them to learn from the places and creatures they encounter.

Islen Waterseer teaches that water brings rebirth, healing and renewal when pure, but can devastate when polluted. He guides shaman trainees through water rites involving Brine’s sapta and the corrupted shrine in Silverpine. He praises the water spirits and trusts a trainee’s noble intent, while warning that the Shadow Council is dangerous.

Kranal Fiss teaches the ways of fire and oversees the fire-sapta rite. He warns that power and destruction come easily, but stresses patience and knowing when to stay one’s hand. He also tells Okla not to stray far from home.

Grunt Dogran is devoted to his mate, Zankaja, and fears his lasting injuries will leave her bound to care for an invalid. He asks that she not be told of his despair, and hopes to die in battle rather than become a lifeless husk. After captivity and grave wounds, he says the draught gives him enough strength to hobble away, though he expects to lose the use of his leg and arm.

Grunt Logmar is concerned for the gravely wounded Dogran and is eager to get the draught to him. With most of the grunts away on a foraging mission, he says they need to get it out to Dogran right away.
Yonada sells tailoring and leatherworking supplies.
Slimeshell Makrura is a makrura creature found in several areas near the Barrens and Durotar. Master Vornal in Sen'jin Village, an alchemist, wants intact makrura eyes from makrura like it.
A humanoid known as Razorfen Servitor in The Barrens.

Klannoc Macleod, called the Islander, is Fray Island's chief warrior and offers instruction to rising warriors. He sets the Affray as a test of their mettle: Twiggy Flathead runs the bouts, and Klannoc welcomes those who pass as worthy students.

Takar the Seer uses his sight to guide a warlock seeking the Heartswood. He recounts how Anathera and Latherion, lovers who fought together against the Legion, died at Hyjal; the tree that grew where they fell is the lure needed for the succubus ritual. His account links the task to the lovers’ story.

Doan Karhan has devoted his life to studying the Burning Legion’s orbs and learning to recreate them. He asks for the scattered pieces of Soran’ruk, explaining their history and the demons’ imprisoned spirits, then reforms the orb and returns it in a form the seeker chooses. He also draws on years spent collecting pieces of another orb, Zargain.

Known as the Announcer, Twiggy Flathead coordinates the Affray on Fray Island. When the challenge begins, he calls a participant into the fray and announces when a challenger falls; he also declares the Affray over. A prospective fighter signals readiness by stepping onto the grate in the crowd.

The Affray Spectators are part of the crowd around Fray Island’s fighting challenge. They watch as challengers take on the Affray, while the announcer calls participants into the fray and reports when one falls. This entry represents a group of spectators rather than a named individual.

Strahad Farsan is a warlock mentor who organizes the Cabal training for summoning a felhunter. He explains the ritual, begins the basic circle, and directs his acolytes to use channeling rods to form the greater circle before the summoning. He warns students that a felhunter is dangerous and speaks from his own experience of barely surviving the encounter. He encourages a successful student’s potential as a warlock.
Acolyte Magaz is a named acolyte in Ratchet. His available conditional advice urges students to heed their elders and says strength of will and dedication can help them control power.
Acolyte Fenrick is an acolyte in the Barrens.

Acolyte Wytula guides warlock students who choose the felhound-soul path in Menara Voidrender's training. Wytula gives them a ruby for capturing a felhound's spirit and sends them to seek felhounds in Desolace; the captured spirit and ruby are brought back to Menara.

Menara Voidrender trains warlocks from Strahad Farsan's tower in Ratchet, directing students through either infernal or felhound paths and judging their choices by their strengths and weaknesses. She also guides them through gathering and crafting enchanted robes and orbs, with attention to the tools that suit their skills. Stern and guarded, she warns strangers against disrespect and meddling with what they do not understand. Her work with Tabetha rests on a history between them: Menara sends students to her to cleanse an infernal orb, and Tabetha later sends them back with it.
Dranh serves as Camp Taurajo’s skinning trainer. His role in the camp is practical and training-focused.

Ruga Ragetotem puts warriors through a timed trial at the Field of Giants, where he asks them to bring back still-twitching antennae from the unfamiliar crawling insects. He distrusts what their arrival may herald and insists on haste. Passing the trial marks another step in a warrior's path; Ruga's next offered step is to speak with Thun'grim Firegaze, a renowned orc blacksmith who wants to fashion armor for them.

Tazan is a troll who trades with the pirates near Ratchet and holds information sought by Therzok's Shattered Hand. Therzok's assignment places Tazan in the order's covert effort to rebuild Horde strength.
Overseer Glibby is the Venture Company's overseer at the Sludge Fen. Rokar Bladeshadow views the company's work as a threat to the land and calls for Glibby's removal to hamper its operation.
Lord Cyrik Blackforge is a humanoid lord at the Keep. He carries Nitroglycerin and Sodium Nitrate, which Gann Stonespire wants to make an explosive charge against the dwarves.

Innkeeper Wiley welcomes travelers and offers lodging and goods. His greeting includes a practical warning about the stove, which he says has not exploded yet that day. His inn also handles a seasonal trick-or-treat interaction.

Wrenix sends adventurers after Southsea treasure aboard the Tide Razor, warning that earlier thieves he sent did not return intact. His dry relief when a returnee still has all their body parts, and his surprise at a successful haul, show how dangerous he considers the job. He also expects another recruit from Zando'zan to face the same danger.

Taskmaster Fizzule is the Shattered Hand's covert operative embedded in the Venture Co. His recognition protocol is exact: signal with two flares, then give the Shattered Hand salute; he attacks those he does not recognize. Once contact is established, he gives an ally a whistle signal for future meetings. His undercover role makes caution central to dealing with him.

Foreman Silixiz is the Venture Co. foreman tied to the tower key sought in Shenthul's operation. The mission calls for stealing the key from him and keeping it for possible later use, making Silixiz a practical obstacle to that covert work.

Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix is a high-value figure in the Venture Co. tower operation. Shenthul's mission specifically calls for his assassination and the taking of his head, alongside a break-in at his lockbox for a cache.
A Venture Co. Lookout fills a watch role among the company's tower force. Shenthul's mission counts two lookouts among the tower inhabitants marked for elimination.
A Venture Co. Patroller serves in the company's tower security force. Shenthul's mission counts two patrollers among the targets there, distinguishing their patrol role from the lookouts.
A Mutated Venture Co. Drone is one of the tower inhabitants singled out in Shenthul's mission, which calls for two drones to be killed and says poison has weakened everything inside.
Innkeeper Byula welcomes visitors with a plains-wind greeting and offers the ordinary hospitality of an innkeeper. Visitors can make the inn their home and browse goods.
Death's Head Cultists are among the growing ranks gathered around the diplomat near Razorfen Downs, whom Myriam Moonsinger fears. This cultist casts Shadow Bolt and Death & Decay.
Razorfen Battleguards are among the growing ranks gathered around the diplomat near Razorfen Downs, whom Myriam Moonsinger fears. This battleguard strikes with heavy Slam blows.

Razorfen Thornweavers are among the growing ranks gathered around the diplomat near Razorfen Downs, whom Myriam Moonsinger fears. This thornweaver wraps itself in Thorns Aura and heals itself with Healing Touch when badly hurt.
Ambassador Bloodrage is an undead ambassador in the Razorfen area.
Barrens Guard is a sentry posted around the Crossroads area of the Barrens.
Zikkel is a banker in the Barrens who gives visitors access to the bank.
Jaxxil Sparks is a vendor who sells fireworks for holiday celebrations.
Muck Frenzy is a beast found in the waters around the Wailing Caverns area. When badly wounded, it turns desperate.
Duhng is a cook who trains others in cooking.
Tarban Hearthgrain is a Baker who sells goods.

Falla Sagewind recognizes the Glowing Shard as a brilliant green crystal with smoke-like swirls beneath its surface. Its vision seems to her more like a nightmare than a dream, and she urges that it be brought to a wise druid, directing Horde and Alliance travelers to Hamuul Runetotem or Mathrengyl Bearwalker. She admits she cannot explain more and reacts with surprise at the shard.

Liv Rizzlefix is an apprentice inventor who admires Marvon Rivetseeker. While he is away studying ancient troll ruins in Tanaris, she works on experiments of her own in his Ratchet workshop. Her projects include a prototype bug zapper and studying Un'Goro's volcanic ash; she is eager to learn from her findings and share them.

Kadrak directs Horde operations from the northern Barrens watchtower, coordinating reports from scouts and outriders in Ashenvale. He treats the reports as crucial to planning the campaign’s next move and says recent Horde efforts have established outposts at Zoram Strand and Splintertree. He also answers the threat posed by Rynthariel of the Talon Den with orders to remove her and warn off further Alliance messengers.

Vazario Linkgrease is a Goblin Engineering trainer who checks for a valid membership card before granting access to goblin engineering schemata. He also handles renewals: the stated fee is two gold, and a renewed card lasts two weeks before dues are owed again.

Wenikee Boltbucket is a curious, hands-on tinkerer who eagerly takes up the challenge of repairing an unfamiliar samophlange. She studies its gears and motion, experiments with gauges, and recognizes that her additions have left it in worse shape. She seeks nugget slugs for further work and points the damaged device toward Rilli Greasygob, whose Venture Company experience she trusts.

Boss Copperplug is a Venture Company boss who hoarded the secrets of the samophlange, giving out only small bits of knowledge to those he trusted. He used to stay at Boulder Lode Mine in the northeastern Barrens. Rilli Greasygob, his former rival, wants his manual.
Grimble is the Shipmaster of the Maiden's Fancy, a passenger ship crossing the Great Sea. He describes the route to Stranglethorn and explains that passengers board when the ship arrives.
Sikwa is a stable master in the Barrens. She offers pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.
Kelsuwa is a stable master in the Barrens. She offers pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.
Lanti'gah recalls that this place was the site of a great battle, then adds that there were many great battles.
Reggifuz is a stable master in the Barrens. He offers pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.

Omusa Thunderhorn is a wind rider master at Camp Taurajo. Though she acknowledges the Crossroads as a center of activity, she prefers Taurajo's quietude. Her travel greetings invoke the Earth Mother and ancestors. When attacked, she summons an enraged wyvern.
Sanuye Runetotem sells leather armor and repairs equipment.
A pack kodo is a beast of burden and herd animal. This entry represents pack kodos found in more than one part of the Barrens.

Makaba Flathoof survived the Grimtotem raid that killed most of his village, and wants more of the clan dead, above all their leader Grundig Darkcloud, who led the attack. He was glad Kaya was rescued and had her aunt, Tammra Windfield at Sun Rock Retreat, told she is alive. He stays near southeastern Stonetalon, urging others against the Grimtotem.
Koiter is a humanoid in The Barrens.
A sickly gazelle is a weak, diseased wild animal found across several parts of the Barrens.
Ambassador Malcin serves the Lich King's mission near Razorfen Downs. This hostile spellcaster wields Shadow Bolt and Curse of Blood.

Myriam Moonsinger is a Forsaken scout studying the quilboar near Razorfen Downs. Troubled by an ominous emanation and an undead diplomat she suspects belongs to the Scourge, she seeks help against the growing ranks around him and continues her investigation.
A veteran Horde soldier who hands out assignments to visitors.
A Horde laborer whose emote calls for help.

Kelm Hargunth is the Warsong supply officer. He gives care packages of rations and bandages to those who begin proving themselves to the Warsong, and sells such supplies for use in Warsong Gulch as trust grows.

Captain Shatterskull is responsible for protecting the Horde’s lumber gathering in Ashenvale. He speaks of the effort as a cause worth fighting for and expects the night elves and their allies to resist.
Gruk serves food, checking whether a guest wants more and bringing bread when asked. He responds promptly and deferentially to requests.

Erk is a young fisherman who misplaces his hook, looks to his father’s wagon for better bait, and tries Quillboar scraps. When he catches a fish, he offers it to the guards and calls for Fang to come along.
Guard Taruc is served bread by a boy. He asks for more, then dismisses the boy once he has had enough.
Trok is being pursued by bees and is exhausted from running. He asks Karu for help, admits he did not realize the bees disliked fire, and pleads for relief from their stings.

Okla gathers colorful and sharp rocks for a necklace, choosing some that catch her eye and imagining how a sharp stone might help her friend Gruk make a spear. She asks Papa before collecting more and promises to be careful. Once she has enough rocks, she thinks it is time to head home.

Karu looks after food for herself and Trok, offering him a meal and teasing him when he refuses it. She also wonders whether the pigs are hungry and asks what happened to them when they are gone. Her talk links everyday care for Trok and the pigs with the work of keeping their household fed.
Fang is a critter in the Barrens.

Guard Kurall is a guard who thanks a boy for a fine catch and says it brings honor to the Horde. His response treats the catch as a contribution worthy of recognition and speaks warmly of the people it honors.
A swarm of bees in The Barrens.
A humanoid peon in the Barrens.

Mogg is a young Horde child who wants to become a warrior like his absent father. He practices by challenging a harpy, treating the encounter as a play-fight and boasting about the Horde as he sends it away.

Pooka calls Mogg inside because it is unsafe while his father is away. The exchange shows Pooka’s concern for the child and their awareness of the family’s absent father; it does not establish Pooka’s relationship to Mogg.
Hecht Copperpinch is a vendor for Smokywood Pastures who sells seasonal goods.

Elder Windtotem is associated with an elder-homage tradition: the elder accepts homage and offers a token, while reflecting on the past importance of hunting for glory and honor. The elder also invites questions about where to find other elders.

Elder High Mountain is associated with an elder-homage tradition: he accepts homage and offers a token, while reflecting on the past importance of hunting for glory and honor. Visitors can ask him about other elders.

Elder Moonwarden speaks of the stars as beacons of hope and strength for ages to come. The elder also points visitors toward other elders, including Bloodhoof, High Mountain, Morningdew, Runetotem, and Windtotem.
Bragok is a flight master who sends travelers to the places they wish to fly.

Mupsi Shacklefridd is a guarded Ratchet contact, warning visitors against causing trouble. Mupsi addresses a former wrongdoer as a possible scoundrel, yet offers a chance to help wounded people after an encounter with the Bloodsail Buccaneers by bringing linen and empty vials. The appeal frames aid as a way to prove a change of ways.
Gargok is the Warsong Gulch battlemaster. He sends fighters against the wretched Alliance there, and turns away those not yet seasoned enough.

Babagaya Shadowcleft is a warlock trainer who warns that the arcane corrupts the weak and tells those she rejects that darkness does not embrace them. Her words are stern and dismissive, framing warlock training in terms of discipline and the dangers of corruption.

Matero Zeshuwal guides skilled warlocks toward binding a dreadsteed, sending them to Mor'zul Bloodbringer, camped near the Altar of Storms in the Burning Steppes. He warns that the ritual is perilous and demands great power and resources.
Nagulon is a demon, the minion of Matero Zeshuwal.

The Barrens Flame Keeper welcomes visitors to honor the Barrens flame and encourages honoring festival fires in Horde settlements. The Keeper also urges the desecration of Alliance fires, expressing hostility toward the Alliance's festival observances.

place_records.text: You are in The Barrens, Horde land in Kalimdor. It is dry savannah dotted with oases, and the Horde holds its main settlements here: Camp Taurajo, The Crossroads, Ratchet and Mor'shan Base Camp. Kolkar centaurs threaten the Horde's holdings, Razormane quilboar attack the supply lines, and Sunscale raptors, prowlers, hyenas and plainstriders roam the open country.

You are in Bael Modan, an excavation site in the Barrens where Bael'dun excavators dig under Alliance guard. Prospector Khazgorm of the Explorers' League sells goods there, and Captain Gerogg Hammertoe commands the guard. Feegly the Exiled still demands the Tear of the Moons, which General Twinbraid locked away in the Keep.

You are in Camp Taurajo, a Horde camp in the Barrens with a flight master, an inn, a stable, and trainers of leatherworking and tailoring. Jorn Skyseer guides hunters through trials against the beasts of the Barrens, and the captive Razormane Mangletooth bargains with the Horde for help against rival quilboar. Stormsnout thunder lizards roam the plains nearby.

You are in Far Watch Post, a Horde outpost in the Barrens. Kargal Battlescar handles recruitment for Barrens duty here, and Ak'Zeloth, who assists Neeru, prepares power stones against the Demon Seed, a Burning Legion tool on Dreadmist Peak.

You are in the Crossroads, a Horde settlement in the Barrens where Thork leads the defenses in the Warchief's name. Razormane attacks have put its supply lines under pressure, and Mankrik remains here, grieving his missing wife and seeking revenge against the quilboars. Devrak runs the wind rider service to Orgrimmar and Thunder Bluff, and Sergra Darkthorn trains hunters on the surrounding plains.
You are in Boulder Lode Mine, a mine in the Barrens where Venture Company enforcers and overseers are the danger.

You are in The Sludge Fen, where Wizzlecrank sits in a stolen goblin shredder he is still learning to operate. Venture Company drudgers and mercenaries are the dangers here, and Supervisor Lugwizzle is a notable hostile overseer.
You are in The Dry Hills, a dry stretch of the Barrens haunted by Witchwing harpies. Witchwing slayers, windcallers and roguefeathers attack travelers alongside plainstriders and prowlers.

You are in Dreadmist Peak, a peak in the Barrens where the Demon Seed rests in a cave above a demonic altar of fire. Burning Blade bruisers and acolytes are the dangers here, and Sarilus Foulborne, an undead mage whom Sentinel Velene Starstrike accuses of defiling water elementals, is found here.

You are in Northwatch Hold, an Alliance fort on the Barrens coast, where Captain Fairmount commands Theramore Marines and Preservers. Cannoneer Smythe fires at the slightest sighting, and Gilthares Firebough, a Ratchet deckhand whose ship sank, is held here and asks to be taken back to Ratchet.

You are in The Forgotten Pools, a Barrens oasis where Kolkar centaur wranglers and stormers are the dangers. Barak Kodobane, a Kolkar leader, camps nearby, and Hecklefang hyenas and Sunscale screechers roam the pools.
You are in Lushwater Oasis, where the Kolkar centaur leader Hezrul Bloodmark leads his people. Oasis snapjaws, Kolkar wranglers, stormers and bloodchargers, and hecklefang hyenas add to the danger.
You are in The Stagnant Oasis, where the centaur Verog the Dervish is based at a command tent. Kolkar marauders, pack runners and bloodchargers, along with oasis snapjaws, are the dangers here.

You are in Field of Giants, grassland in the Barrens. Silithid swarmers, creepers and grubs roam its open ground, with stormhides and hecklefang stalkers among them. A zhevra courser ranges the grasslands here and can lash out when threatened.

You are in The Merchant Coast, a stretch of Barrens shoreline. Southsea brigands and cannoneers raid along the shore, and Baron Longshore is a notable threat here. Slimeshell makrura and sand sharks are dangerous to travelers as well.

You are in Ratchet, a goblin port on the Barrens coast that the Horde counts among its settlements. Most of its people are neutral, a mix of tinkers and traders. Gazlowe runs a trading operation here and is angry that Southsea Freebooters keep raiding his ships. Its inn and bank serve travelers.

You are in The Tidus Stair, a stretch of Barrens coast. Mahren Skyseer hunts the great water beasts along this coast and calls them worthy prey. Islen Waterseer teaches water rites to shaman trainees.
You are in Gold Road, a Barrens road. Hecklefang hyenas, savannah huntresses and sunscale screechers roam along it. Horde guards are posted here.

You are in Fray Island, a warriors' island. Klannoc Macleod, called the Islander, teaches rising warriors and sets them a challenge called the Affray. Twiggy Flathead announces the bouts. Muck frenzies also haunt the island.

You are in Southfury River, a Barrens waterway that the Horde keeps watch over. Dreadmaw crocolisks, some of them corrupted, haunt its banks, and hecklefang hyenas roam nearby. An Orgrimmar grunt helps visitors find the bank and inn.

You are in Southern Barrens, a broad stretch of the Barrens where Alliance outrunners work alongside neutral kodos. Thunderheads, stormhides and hecklefang stalkers roam its grass. Doan Karhan studies the orbs of the Burning Legion here, and Takar the Seer uses his sight to guide a warlock.

You are in Southern Gold Road, a Barrens road where Gann Stonespire walks alone. He regards the dwarven excavation at Bael Modan as a violation of his tribe's land, and he works to halt its destruction.

You are in Razorfen Downs, where quilboar and Death's Head cultists gather in growing numbers. Myriam Moonsinger, a Forsaken scout, studies them and is troubled by an undead diplomat she suspects belongs to the Scourge. Razorfen battleguards, thornweavers and galak marauders are the dangers here.
You are in Mor'shan Base Camp, a Horde camp in the Barrens with a Warsong battlemaster and repairs. Kelm Hargunth, the Warsong supply officer, hands out rations and bandages here.
You are in Raptor Grounds, a stretch of the Barrens where sunscale scytheclaws and ornery plainstriders roam.

You are in Bramblescar, a stretch of the Barrens. Wandering giraffes roam its grasslands and lash out when threatened. Bristleback thornweavers, geomancers and hunters, along with Sunscale scytheclaws, roam the area and make it dangerous.

You are in Thorn Hill, a hill in the Barrens. Fleeting plainstriders and Barrens giraffes roam it, and both can answer an attack with a spell. Razormane defenders, geomancers, hunters and mystics make the hill dangerous.

You are in Agama'gor, a place in the Barrens. Grunt Dogran, of the Horde, is devoted to his mate Zankaja and fears his injuries will leave her caring for an invalid, so he asks that she not be told of his despair. Venture Co. workers and supervisors, Bristleback hunters and geomancers, and Stormsnouts make it dangerous.

You are in Blackthorn Ridge, a ridge in the Barrens with a spirit healer. Brine, a Horde woman who studies water, lives alone in a hut deep in the Barrens and treasures the scarce pond below her hut. Razormane seers and stalkers, greater thunderhawks and stormhides make the ridge dangerous, and kodos charge in combat.

You are in Honor's Stand, a spot in the Barrens. A Barrens Guard, a Horde sentry posted around the Crossroads, is among the people here, and kodos and giraffes wander the area. Ornery plainstriders, Sunscale scytheclaws and Sunscale screechers are its dangers.

You are in The Mor'shan Rampart, a place in the Barrens where Horde people are stationed. Kadrak directs Horde operations, gathering reports from scouts and outriders in Ashenvale. Ashenvale bears are the local danger.

You are in Grol'dom Farm, a farm in the Barrens where several Horde people are. Kranal Fiss teaches the ways of fire and oversees the fire-sapta rite, warning that power comes easily but patience must guide it. Trok runs from a swarm of bees here, and Sunscale screechers are a danger.
You are in The Great Sea. A transport here runs to Booty Bay.
You are in the Shrine of the Fallen Warrior, a shrine in the Barrens. Fleeting plainstriders range through it and can answer a threat with a spell. A humanoid named Koiter is also here.

You are in Bael'dun Keep, an Alliance-held keep in the Barrens. Captain Gerogg Hammertoe commands its guard, and Bael'dun soldiers and riflemen keep the place under arms. Malgin Barleybrew, the morale officer, sells goods to visitors.
